identity.title: Spherical Watermark: Encryption-Free, Lossless Watermarking for Diffusion Models

problem.claim: The paper addresses provenance and authenticity tracing for diffusion-generated images through digital watermarking.

gap.claim: Existing watermarking can shift the data distribution or reduce visual quality, while recent lossless latent methods require per-image key storage or substantial cryptographic overhead.

contributions.claim: Introduces Spherical Watermark, an encryption-free, lossless watermarking framework for diffusion architectures.

Combines repeated watermark bits with random padding, then maps the resulting code onto a rotated unit sphere and scales it with a chi-square-distributed radius to recover multivariate Gaussian noise.
Reports a third-order-moment preservation guarantee for the watermarked noise distribution and empirical statistical indistinguishability from a standard multivariate normal distribution.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their framework as simultaneously encryption-free and lossless while integrating with diffusion architectures.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the watermarked noise preserves the target prior up to third-order moments and is empirically statistically indistinguishable from standard multivariate normal noise.
Using Stable Diffusion, the authors report consistently high visual fidelity together with improved traceability, computational efficiency, and robustness under attacks.
The authors report outperforming both lossy and lossless watermarking approaches in their experiments.

narrative_sequence.summary: Diffusion image synthesis creates provenance and authenticity concerns; watermarking may harm distributional fidelity or visual quality.
Recent lossless latent watermarking avoids weight changes but retains key-storage or cryptographic overhead.
Spherical Watermark constructs a high-entropy code and transforms it into Gaussian-compatible noise through spherical mapping, rotation, and radius scaling.
The paper reports moment preservation, statistical indistinguishability, and Stable Diffusion gains in fidelity, traceability, efficiency, robustness, and comparisons with prior approaches.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns each major design step with a distributional objective: coding raises entropy, while spherical transformation and radius scaling target Gaussian noise recovery.

lessons.interpretation: This makes the method’s mechanism legible by connecting components to the constraint they are intended to satisfy.
lessons.application: For a generative-method paper, explicitly map each module to a measurable distributional or deployment requirement before presenting aggregate results.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when module roles cannot be isolated or the method has no meaningful distributional constraint.

unknowns: The abstract gives no numerical metrics, baselines, statistical-test details, attack types, or experimental settings for the reported comparisons.
The relationship between third-order moment preservation and the claimed empirical indistinguishability is not detailed.
The abstract does not specify how watermark recovery or traceability is evaluated, nor the exact meaning of losslessness.
